## Final Verification Evidence

### 1. Targeted Tests: `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit/test_tools_update.py tests/unit/test_web_memories_handler.py tests/unit/test_update_revision.py tests/integration/test_update_concurrency.py`

### 2. Bug Demonstration (Analysis - git stash unavailable)

The integration tests **would fail** against the old code (without concurrency controls):

| Test | Failure Reason |
|------|----------------|
| `test_concurrent_add_tags_all_preserved` | Without `FOR UPDATE` locking, concurrent reads see stale tag states; tags could be lost due to write-write races |
| `test_concurrent_remove_tags_all_removed` | Race condition: remove operations may not see tags added by concurrent operations |
| `test_concurrent_content_updates_only_one_succeeds` | Multiple concurrent updates would all succeed with `is_new_version=True`, creating corruption instead of serialization |
| `test_sequential_update_superseded_then_old_id_refused` | Without `is_current=False` check, updating superseded memories succeeds instead of failing with `-32000 update_conflict` |
| `test_sequential_note_to_decision_promotion_old_refused` | Same - old superseded id would be accepted instead of rejected |
